name: FC Dinamo Tbilisi
content:
FC Dinamo Tbilisi is a professional football club based in Tbilisi, Georgia, founded in 1925. It competes in the top division of Georgian football, the Erovnuli Liga, and plays its home matches at the Boris Paichadze Dinamo Arena. The club has long been one of the most prominent and successful teams in the country, with a strong historical identity linked to the Dynamo sports society during the Soviet era.

During the Soviet period, Dinamo Tbilisi was among the leading clubs in the Soviet Top League and was notable for never being relegated. Its greatest achievement came in 1981, when the team won the European Cup Winners’ Cup by defeating Carl Zeiss Jena in the final, becoming the only Georgian club to win a major European trophy. The club also won the Soviet league title in 1978 and multiple domestic cups, with legendary coach Nodar Akhalkatsi playing a key role in its success.

After the dissolution of the Soviet Union, Dinamo Tbilisi continued its dominance domestically, becoming the most successful club in independent Georgia with numerous league titles and cup victories. The club has also developed many notable players who later achieved international recognition. Despite fluctuating results in European competitions in recent years, Dinamo Tbilisi remains a central institution in Georgian football and a symbol of the country’s sporting history.

name: FC Torpedo Kutaisi
content:
FC Torpedo Kutaisi is a professional football club based in Kutaisi, one of the largest cities in Georgia. Founded in 1946, the team competes in the Erovnuli Liga, the top tier of Georgian football, and plays its home matches at the Ramaz Shengelia Stadium. The club is considered one of the most historically significant in the country and has maintained a strong presence in the top division for most of its existence.

During the Soviet era, Torpedo Kutaisi regularly participated in the Soviet league system, including spells in the top division, and developed many notable players. After Georgia gained independence, the club became one of the leading forces in national football, winning multiple league titles, particularly dominating in the early 2000s with three consecutive championships.

Overall, Torpedo Kutaisi is regarded as the second most successful club in Georgian football history. It has won several domestic trophies, including league titles, national cups, and super cups, and has also appeared in European competitions. Despite occasional financial and sporting difficulties, the club remains an important part of Georgian football culture and tradition.

name: FC Iberia 1999
content:
FC Iberia 1999 is a professional football club based in Tbilisi, Georgia. Founded in 1999, the team was originally known as FC Saburtalo, named after the district where it is located. The club competes in the Erovnuli Liga, the top division of Georgian football, and plays its home matches at a small local stadium in the capital. It is also known for having one of the strongest youth academies in the country.

The club experienced steady growth after being acquired by Iberia Business Group in 2005. Its major breakthrough came in the mid-2010s, when it won promotion to the top tier and quickly became competitive. In 2018, the team won its first national league title, followed by success in domestic cup competitions and a Super Cup victory. These achievements established the club as one of the leading teams in modern Georgian football.

In recent years, Iberia 1999 has continued to collect domestic trophies, including additional league titles and cup wins, and has represented Georgia in European competitions. In 2024, the club officially changed its name from Saburtalo to Iberia 1999, reflecting a new identity while maintaining its connection to local roots. Today, it is regarded as one of the most successful Georgian clubs of the contemporary era.

name: FC Dinamo Batumi
content:
FC Dinamo Batumi is a professional football club based in Batumi, Georgia, founded in 1923. It competes in the Erovnuli Liga, the top division of Georgian football, and plays its home matches at the modern Adjarabet Arena. The club is one of the notable teams in the country and has maintained a consistent presence in the top tier, representing the Adjara region.

During its history, Dinamo Batumi experienced various periods of development, including participation in Soviet competitions before Georgia’s independence. In the early 1990s, the club briefly changed its name to FC Batumi before returning to its traditional identity. Its first major domestic success came in the 1997–98 season, when it won the Georgian Cup and also secured the national Super Cup.

In modern times, Dinamo Batumi has emerged as one of the leading clubs in Georgian football, winning the national league title in 2021 and again in 2023. The team has also been a regular participant in European competitions, representing Georgia on the international stage. With recent domestic successes and improved infrastructure, the club continues to strengthen its position as a major force in the country’s football landscape.

name: FC WIT Georgia
content:
FC WIT Georgia is a professional football club based in Tbilisi, Georgia. Founded in 1997 under its current identity, the club is sponsored by a company specializing in pet products and pharmaceuticals, from which it takes its name. The team has played its home matches in Tbilisi and has competed in various levels of the Georgian league system, currently participating in the lower divisions after previously featuring in the top tier.

The club achieved its greatest success in the 2000s, winning the Georgian national championship twice, in 2003–04 and 2009. It also secured the Georgian Cup in 2010 and the Super Cup in 2009. These achievements allowed WIT Georgia to participate in European competitions, including the UEFA Champions League qualifiers and the UEFA Cup, marking the peak period in the club’s history.

After the 2010–11 season, the club’s performance declined, leading to relegation from the top division in the mid-2010s. Although it later managed to return to higher levels of Georgian football for a period, WIT Georgia has not regained its former status. Despite this, it remains a notable club in Georgian football, remembered for its domestic successes and contributions during its peak years.

name: FC Zestaponi
content:
FC Zestaponi is a professional football club based in the city of Zestaponi, Georgia. Founded in 2004, the club quickly became part of the top tier of Georgian football, joining the Umaglesi Liga soon after its creation. It emerged as a successor to earlier local teams and was closely connected to the city’s industrial background, particularly the ferro-alloy plant that supported its development.

The club achieved its greatest success in the late 2000s and early 2010s, becoming one of the strongest teams in the country. Zestaponi won the Georgian national championship twice, in the 2010–11 and 2011–12 seasons, and also claimed the Georgian Cup earlier in 2007–08. During this period, the team regularly competed in European tournaments, reaching qualifying rounds of both the UEFA Champions League and the UEFA Europa League.

After its peak years, the club experienced a significant decline due to financial and organizational problems. By the mid-2010s, it dropped out of the top division and later competed in lower leagues, even facing relegations in subsequent seasons. Despite these setbacks, FC Zestaponi remains an important part of modern Georgian football history, remembered for its rapid rise and notable domestic achievements.

name: FC Metalurgi Rustavi
content:
FC Metalurgi Rustavi was a professional football club based in Rustavi, Georgia, with roots tracing back to a Soviet-era team known as Metalurgi. After Georgia’s independence, the club underwent several name changes, including Gorda and later Rustavi, while competing in the national league system. For much of the 1990s, the team remained a mid-table side, though it produced several players who later represented the national team.

A major turning point came in 2006 when the club merged with another team and became known as Olimpi Rustavi. This marked the beginning of its most successful period, as it quickly emerged as a title contender and won the Georgian league championship in 2007, followed by another title in 2010. During this era, the club also secured a Super Cup and regularly participated in European competitions, achieving some success in qualifying rounds.

In 2011, the club returned to the name Metalurgi Rustavi, but its fortunes declined in the following years. Financial problems severely affected the team, leading to poor results, relegation, and eventually withdrawal from competition during the 2015–16 season. The club was declared bankrupt soon after, marking the end of its existence, although a new team later emerged in Rustavi without legal continuity.

name: FC Dila Gori
content:
FC Dila Gori is a professional football club based in the city of Gori, Georgia. Founded in 1949, the team competes in the Erovnuli Liga, the top division of Georgian football, and plays its home matches at the Tengiz Burjanadze Stadium. The club has a long history and is one of the established teams representing central Georgia in national competitions.

During the Soviet era, Dila Gori mostly played in the lower divisions of the Soviet league system, achieving its best results in the third tier. After Georgia gained independence, the club experienced fluctuating fortunes, moving between divisions before stabilizing in the top league in the early 2010s. Its breakthrough came in 2012 when it won the Georgian Cup, marking its first major national trophy.

The club reached its peak in the 2014–15 season by winning the Georgian national championship for the first time. Since then, Dila Gori has remained competitive domestically, regularly finishing near the top of the league and participating in European competitions. With multiple domestic trophies and consistent performances in recent years, it is regarded as a strong and stable club in modern Georgian football.

name: FC Samtredia
content:
FC Samtredia is a professional football club based in the city of Samtredia, Georgia. Founded in 1936 as Sanavardo Samtredia, the club has undergone several name changes throughout its history before returning to its current name in 2006. It plays its home matches at the Erosi Manjgaladze Stadium and currently competes in Erovnuli Liga 2, the second tier of Georgian football.

After Georgia gained independence, Samtredia became a regular participant in the national top division, achieving its best early result with a runner-up finish in the 1994–95 season. The club also made its debut in European competitions during this period, although it did not progress far. In the following years, Samtredia experienced fluctuations between divisions, including relegations and promotions, reflecting an inconsistent sporting trajectory.

The most successful period in the club’s history came in the mid-2010s. In 2016, Samtredia won its first Georgian league title and followed it with a Super Cup victory, marking the peak of its achievements. Since then, the club has continued to compete domestically but has not consistently maintained top-tier status, though it remains a recognized name in Georgian football.

name: FC Sioni Bolnisi
content:
FC Sioni Bolnisi is a professional football club based in the city of Bolnisi, Georgia. Founded in 1936, it is one of the older clubs in the country and currently competes in Erovnuli Liga 2, the second tier of Georgian football. The team plays its home matches at the Tamaz Stepania Stadium and takes its name from a historic local cathedral, reflecting its regional identity.

For many years, Sioni alternated between lower divisions before establishing itself in the top league in the mid-1990s. The club came close to winning the national title in the 2003–04 season, finishing level on points with the leaders but losing a decisive playoff match. Its greatest achievement followed shortly after, when Sioni won the Georgian championship in the 2005–06 season, marking the peak of its success.

Sioni has also reached the final of the Georgian Cup on multiple occasions and participated in European competitions, including qualifying rounds of the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Cup. In more recent years, the club has spent time outside the top division, competing in the second tier while aiming to return to higher levels. Despite fluctuations in performance, it remains a recognized name in Georgian football history.

name: FC Chikhura Sachkhere
content:
FC Chikhura Sachkhere is a Georgian football club based in the town of Sachkhere. Founded in 1938, the club spent much of its early history in lower divisions and experienced several periods of inactivity and reformation. For decades it remained a modest regional team before gradually rising into the national league system after Georgia’s independence.

The club’s most successful period came in the 2010s, when it established itself as a competitive top-flight side. Chikhura reached its first major milestone in 2013 by playing in the Georgian Cup final, which also earned it qualification for European competitions. It later achieved one of its most notable international results by defeating stronger opponents in the UEFA Europa League qualifiers, gaining recognition for its disciplined and hardworking style.

Domestically, Chikhura won the Georgian Cup in 2017 and the Super Cup in 2013, marking the peak of its achievements. The club also came close to winning the national league in 2016, finishing near the top but falling short in the decisive stages. In recent years, however, it has faced financial and sporting difficulties, resulting in relegations to lower divisions, though it remains part of the Georgian football structure.

name: FC Ameri Tbilisi
content:
FC Ameri Tbilisi was a professional football club based in Tbilisi, Georgia. It was founded in 2002 and represented a short-lived but successful project in Georgian football. The club quickly progressed through the league system, establishing itself as a competitive side in the country’s top division.

The peak of Ameri’s success came in the mid-2000s. The club won the Georgian Cup twice, in 2006 and 2007, and also secured back-to-back Georgian Super Cup titles during the same period. These achievements allowed the team to participate in European competitions, including UEFA Cup qualifying rounds, where it faced stronger international opponents.

Despite its early success, FC Ameri Tbilisi was dissolved in 2009 due to financial difficulties. Although its existence was brief, the club is remembered for its rapid rise, domestic trophy wins, and appearance on the European stage, making it one of the notable short-lived teams in Georgian football history.

name: FC Tbilisi
content:
FC Tbilisi was a professional football club based in the capital city of Georgia, Tbilisi. The club was founded in 1991 and went through several name changes and reorganizations during its existence. It played its home matches in local stadiums and competed in the top tiers of Georgian football during different periods of its history.

Throughout its existence, FC Tbilisi experienced mixed sporting success. The team competed in the Georgian top division in the early and mid-2000s, achieving solid league finishes, including a third-place result in the 2004–05 season. It also took part in European competitions, where it faced stronger clubs in the qualifying rounds but did not advance far.

The club underwent mergers and structural changes, including a period when it became part of a combined project that later evolved into Olimpi Rustavi. After separating again, FC Tbilisi struggled to maintain stability and eventually ceased operations in 2009. Despite its relatively short and fragmented history, it is remembered as part of the early post-independence era of Georgian club football.

name: FC Locomotive Tbilisi
content:
FC Locomotive Tbilisi is a professional football club based in Tbilisi, Georgia. Founded on 14 August 1936, it was originally part of the Soviet railway sports society and has long-standing ties with the Georgian railway system. The club competes in the Georgian football league system and plays its home matches at the Mikheil Meskhi Stadium.

During the Soviet era, Locomotive participated across multiple divisions, including brief appearances in the top league in the late 1930s and 1940. In the post-Soviet period, the club became a regular participant in Georgia’s top flight. Its most successful domestic period came around the turn of the 2000s, when it finished as runner-up in the national championship twice and won the Georgian Cup three times.

In European competitions, Locomotive has reached qualifying and early knockout rounds of UEFA tournaments, achieving occasional notable wins but generally limited progress. In recent years, the club has fluctuated between the top two divisions of Georgian football. Despite this inconsistency, it remains an important and historic club in the country’s football landscape.

name: FC Kolkheti-1913 Poti
content:
FC Kolkheti-1913 Poti is a professional football club based in the city of Poti, Georgia. Founded in 1913, it is considered one of the oldest active football clubs in the country. The team plays its home matches at Fazisi Stadium and has traditionally been associated with the port city’s sporting identity.

Throughout its history, Kolkheti has experienced both strong periods and long struggles. In the 1990s, it was one of the competitive sides in Georgia’s top division, regularly finishing near the top of the table and even achieving runner-up positions. However, financial difficulties in the 2000s caused instability, leading to relegations and periods spent in lower divisions.

In modern years, the club has continued to move between divisions, working to regain stability and consistency. It has spent recent seasons mainly in the lower tiers of Georgian football, but remains an important historic team due to its long legacy and early role in the country’s football development.

name: FC Margveti Zestaponi
content:
FC Margveti Zestaponi was a Georgian football club based in the city of Zestaponi. It was founded in 1990, at the beginning of Georgia’s independent national football system after the collapse of the Soviet league structure. The club quickly became part of the country’s top division and represented the early development of professional football in post-Soviet Georgia.

During the 1990s, Margveti experienced its strongest period. The team achieved notable results in the Umaglesi Liga, including a runner-up finish in the 1995–96 season, which was the peak of its competitive success. It also reached the later stages of the Georgian Cup on several occasions and even took part in European competition, playing in the UEFA Cup qualifiers.

Despite its sporting achievements, the club struggled financially toward the end of the decade. These difficulties led to a decline in performance and eventual relegation from the top division. FC Margveti Zestaponi was declared bankrupt and dissolved in 2000, ending its short but notable presence in Georgian football history.

name: FC Alazani Gurjaani
content:
FC Alazani Gurjaani is a Georgian football club based in the town of Gurjaani in the Kakheti region. Founded in 1964 during the Soviet period, the club has long represented one of the main sporting sides in the area. It plays its home matches at the David Kipiani Stadium and has mostly competed in the Georgian league system’s lower and mid tiers.

The club’s most successful period came in the early 1990s, shortly after Georgia gained independence. In the 1992–93 season, Alazani achieved its best-ever league result by finishing third in the top division, marking a peak in its competitive history. During this era, the team also went through several name changes before settling on its current identity.

In later years, Alazani Gurjaani moved between divisions and spent significant time in lower leagues, including regional competitions. While it has not repeated its early top-flight success, the club has remained active in Georgian football and continues to compete at semi-professional and lower professional levels, maintaining its local football tradition.

name: FC Shevardeni-1906 Tbilisi
content:
FC Shevardeni-1906 Tbilisi is a Georgian football club based in Tbilisi. It is widely regarded as one of the oldest football clubs in the country, originally founded in 1906. The club’s early roots are linked to a sports society established in the city during the pre-Soviet period, and it developed through various forms of competition over the 20th century.

During the Soviet era, Shevardeni competed mainly in regional and lower divisions before reaching the Soviet league system in the late 1980s. After Georgia gained independence, the club played in the top division during the 1990s and achieved its best result in the 1992–93 season, finishing as runners-up. Later, it went through mergers with other Tbilisi clubs and temporarily disappeared from the top level.

The club was re-established in the 2010s and gradually climbed back through the Georgian league system, reaching the second tier of professional football. However, in 2022, it was expelled from competition following disciplinary issues, and its results were annulled. Shortly after, the club ceased operations, marking the end of its modern revival.

name: FC Tskhumi Sokhumi
content:
FC Tskhumi Sokhumi is a Georgian football club originally founded in 1990 in the city of Sokhumi. It was created as a breakaway team from Dinamo Sokhumi to represent the city in the newly formed Georgian league system after the collapse of Soviet football structures. The club quickly joined the top division and became one of the early participants in independent Georgian football.

In its early years, Tskhumi achieved strong results, including reaching the final of the Georgian Cup twice and finishing as high as second place in the national league. However, its progress was interrupted by the conflict in Abkhazia in the early 1990s, which forced the club to stop competing and effectively led to its dissolution for several years.

The club was later re-established in Tbilisi by displaced people from Sokhumi and resumed participation in lower divisions of Georgian football. Since its revival, it has mainly competed in regional and lower leagues, without returning to its former top-flight status. Despite this, it remains a symbol of the pre-war football tradition of Sokhumi.

name: FC Guria Lanchkhuti
content:
FC Guria Lanchkhuti is a professional football club based in the town of Lanchkhuti in western Georgia. Founded in 1925, it is one of the most historic clubs in the country and has long represented the Guria region in national competitions. The team plays its home matches at the Evgrapi Shevardnadze Stadium and has been an important part of Georgian football culture for decades.

The club reached its strongest level in the late Soviet period and early years of Georgian independence. During the late 1980s and early 1990s, Guria competed in the Soviet top division and later became a strong side in the national league, finishing as runners-up in the early 1990s. It also won the Georgian Cup in 1990, marking its most significant trophy achievement.

In later years, Guria experienced financial and sporting difficulties, leading to relegations and time spent in lower divisions. Despite this decline, the club has remained active and continues to compete in the Georgian league system, recently appearing in lower tiers while working to rebuild stability and return to higher levels of competition.

name: FC Gagra
content:
FC Gagra is a Georgian football club based in Tbilisi, founded in 2004 by a group of businessmen and former players originally connected to the city of Gagra in Abkhazia. The club was created as a symbol of unity and the hope of returning to its homeland, but due to the ongoing conflict in the region, it has always played its home matches in Tbilisi. It started from the lower tiers of Georgian football and gradually worked its way up through the league system.

The club’s breakthrough came in the 2010–11 season, when it achieved remarkable success by winning both the Georgian Cup and the second division, earning promotion to the top tier. That same period also marked its debut in European competitions, where it represented Georgia in UEFA tournament qualifiers. These achievements made Gagra one of the most notable underdog stories in Georgian football history.

In later years, FC Gagra has moved between divisions, experiencing both promotions and relegations. It has continued to compete in the national league system, maintaining a reputation as a resilient and ambitious club despite limited resources. The team remains active today, still based in Tbilisi and continuing its efforts to return to the highest level of Georgian football.

name: FC Spaeri
content:
FC Spaeri is a professional football club based in Tbilisi, Georgia. It was founded in 2017 by members of the Special State Protection Service and initially consisted mainly of players connected to that organization. The club started in the lowest tiers of Georgian football and gradually progressed through the league system.

In a very short period, Spaeri achieved rapid success. It won multiple lower-division titles, including Liga 4 in 2019 and Liga 3 in 2021, earning promotion each time. The team also established itself as a strong competitor in Liga 2, finishing near the top of the table and repeatedly reaching promotion play-offs. Its steady rise made it one of the fastest-developing clubs in Georgian football.

The club’s biggest achievement came in 2024, when it won the Georgian Cup, defeating a top domestic side in the final. This victory qualified Spaeri for its first participation in European competitions, marking an important milestone in its history. Despite being a relatively new club, Spaeri has quickly gained recognition for its rapid progress and competitive performances.

name: FC Samgurali Tskaltubo
content:
FC Samgurali Tskaltubo is a professional football club based in Tskaltubo, Georgia. Founded in 1945, the club has a long history and is one of the traditional teams in Georgian football. It plays its home matches at the 26 May Stadium and represents the Imereti region.

The club experienced its strongest period during the Soviet era, especially in the 1980s, when it won multiple regional championships and established itself as one of the leading sides in Georgian SSR football. After the creation of the independent Georgian league in 1990, Samgurali became a regular participant in the top division and remained there for most of the early seasons. However, financial and sporting difficulties later caused instability, leading to relegation and even temporary disappearance from competition.

In recent years, Samgurali has rebuilt its position in Georgian football. After being revived and reorganized, the club worked its way back up through the lower divisions and returned to the top tier after a long absence. It now competes in the Erovnuli Liga, aiming to re-establish itself as a stable top-flight team, while continuing its tradition as one of the historic clubs from western Georgia.

name: FC Rustavi
content:
FC Rustavi is a Georgian football club based in the city of Rustavi. The modern version of the club was founded in 2015 and is considered a separate entity from earlier teams that used the Rustavi name. It represents one of the newer projects in Georgian football and competes in the national league system.

Despite its recent foundation, the club quickly progressed through the lower divisions and achieved rapid sporting success. Within a short time, it secured promotions and even reached the top tier of Georgian football. FC Rustavi has also experienced relegations and returns between divisions, reflecting its fluctuating but competitive status in the national system.

In addition to league performances, FC Rustavi has participated in domestic cup competitions, where it has faced some of the strongest teams in the country. The club is still relatively young and continues to develop its structure, aiming to establish long-term stability and become a consistent top-division side in Georgian football.

name: FC Merani Martvili
content:
FC Merani Martvili is a Georgian football club based in the town of Martvili. Founded in 2006, it was established as a modern continuation of earlier local football traditions in the region. The club plays its home matches at the municipal stadium in Martvili and has competed mainly in the lower and second tiers of the Georgian league system.

After its formation, Merani quickly climbed through the divisions, achieving promotion to the top flight in the early 2010s. The club also recorded one of its strongest periods during that time, including a fifth-place finish in its debut season at the highest level. It has participated in domestic cup competitions as well, reaching an unexpected Georgian Cup final in the 2015–16 season, which marked its most notable cup run.

In later years, FC Merani Martvili experienced instability, with several relegations and returns between divisions. Despite financial and sporting challenges, the club has continued to compete in the Georgian league structure and remains active today, often alternating between the second and third tiers while working to regain top-level consistency.
